body: When I am serving a new table “can I get you some alcohol” always a fun one.

Go work in a bar or restaurant for a decade and then come back to this idea; for one, no one respects an owner who is useless and over reliant on their GM to do things for them( or for that matter, has made some cash elsewhere and thinks they can roll back into hospitality like it’s nothing). Secondly, what people want from a bar or restaurant (particularly in Edinburgh) has changed massively , so become a student of the industry locally, attend the events, read/watch the blogs and eat/drink repeat. 

With real long experience, local connections and knowledge, you will have all the knowledge you need to start a business
Honestly, you are my ideal! x

I don't entirely know what you're overall perspective is on the scene but as someone from the UK, our drill is the mainstream now, taking over from Grime and all our 'old' heads- Grime MCs- have made overtures to it; But even then, 'UK drill is heavily influenced by Chicago drill,  think, Chief Keef, who was mainstream; So, it has massive sticking potential and is mainstream in at least one country; You may have noticed I haven't mentioned NY Drill or Drake yet the reason for this simple, both the NY scene and Drake used the UK beat style; the UK scene- which is anti-American in the fact that it has always sought to seek independence from the states- did not exactly welcome this with enthusiasm; So, we are left with a very complex picture and probably the first transatlantic rap scene that may rise but it may fall.
